decks.module: Who may take the road test
decks.domain: Licensing, road test and teen restrictions

cards.front: How many coached road training hours must sixteen- and seventeen-year-old applicants log, and how may they be mixed?
cards.back: Every sixteen and seventeen year old applicant must log at least forty hours of coached road training, mixing professional school lessons and home practice in any share.

cards.front: What must adults of eighteen or more do before any road test?
cards.back: Adults of eighteen or more must get a learner permit and hold it at least ninety days before any road test.

cards.front: Which gate must adults clear before the road test, and which gate must teens clear?
cards.back: Adults wait ninety permit days before the road test, whereas teens log forty road hours first, so the adult gate is time and the teen gate is practice.

cards.front: With whom may an adult permit holder drive?
cards.back: An adult permit holder drives only under teaching and beside a commercial or secondary school instructor or a qualified trainer of twenty plus, licensed with no suspension across four or more straight years before training.

cards.front: Which adults must take the eight-hour safe driving course, and what must they show?
cards.back: Adults never licensed in Connecticut and holding no valid out of state license must take the eight hour safe driving course and show its attendance certificate.

decks.domain: Licensing, road test and teen restrictions

cards.front: What must applicants know before testing?
cards.back: Before testing, applicants must know proper speed, turning and driving lanes, right of way yielding, yellow light stopping, safe backing, and every style of parking including hills and curbs.

cards.front: What should you do before moving the test car?
cards.back: Before moving the test car, follow directions, scan parked cars and people nearby, clear and defog glass and mirrors, and brake before shifting out of park.

cards.front: How should you drive during the road test?
cards.back: During the drive, shift and accelerate smoothly, reach road speed promptly, keep a fitting space cushion, and stop with smooth safe braking.

cards.front: How should you handle signals and turns during the test?
cards.back: Signal every proper turn and show hand signals too, watch traffic and walkers through each turn at a fitting speed, and stay alert with sound judgment throughout.

cards.front: What does the road test score?
cards.back: The road test scores seat and mirror setup, equipment use, sign and signal response with courteous yielding, backing and parking, basic turns, warning light reading, and any extra maneuvers the inspector orders.

decks.domain: Licensing, road test and teen restrictions

cards.front: When do you book the road test, and where do you find test sites?
cards.back: Once the permit time and training stand met, book the road test appointment and find sites at ct.gov slash dmv slash offices.

cards.front: What car and papers must you arrive with for the road test?
cards.back: Arrive in a class fitting, mechanically safe car with valid registration and insurance papers, since an unlicensed driver may not drive there alone.

cards.front: What rules cover leased cars and rental cars for the road test?
cards.back: A long term leased car qualifies only with insurance naming the car and the lease company registrant, and no unlicensed applicant may test in a rental.

cards.front: How does a leased test car differ from a rental car for an unlicensed tester?
cards.back: A leased test car passes only when its insurance names car and lease company, while a rental car fails outright for any unlicensed tester.

cards.front: What happens if the test car is unsafe?
cards.back: An unsafe test car cancels the evaluation and earns a free rescheduled appointment.

decks.module: Papers, fees and the license card
decks.domain: Licensing, road test and teen restrictions

cards.front: What must you bring on road test day, and when is the license fee paid?
cards.back: Road test day needs the learner permit, the CS-one eight hour course proof, an eighty four dollar license fee payable after passing, and any required medical clearance letter.

cards.front: How do sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds prove driver training?
cards.back: Sixteen and seventeen year olds also prove driver training with a home training CS-one, a commercial school certificate, or a secondary school certificate.

cards.front: What parent teaching proof must teens show, and where is it taken?
cards.back: Teens also prove two parent teaching hours on under eighteen law and teen driving perils, taken inside the required eight hour program.

cards.front: Which test day proof does every tester share, and what do teen testers add?
cards.back: Every tester brings the CS-one eight hour proof, but teen testers stack a second training certificate plus parent teaching proof on top.

cards.front: Which payment methods do branch offices take?
cards.back: Branch offices take cash, money orders, personal checks, debit and credit cards, and bank checks, all checks payable to DMV.

cards.front: How do qualifiers get their license card?
cards.back: Qualifiers leave with a temporary paper card while the permanent license card follows by mail within twenty days.

cards.front: Which card do qualifiers carry out of the office, and which one comes later?
cards.back: Qualifiers pocket a temporary paper card at the office the same day, yet the lasting plastic card travels by mail inside twenty days.

decks.module: Teen passenger, curfew and device limits
decks.domain: Licensing, road test and teen restrictions

cards.front: Whom may newly licensed sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds carry during the first six months?
cards.back: Newly licensed sixteen and seventeen year olds carry no passengers for six months except a licensed instructor, a licensed parent or guardian, or one twenty plus person with four straight licensed years and no suspension in the prior four.

cards.front: Which new passengers are allowed in months seven through twelve?
cards.back: In months seven through twelve the only new passengers allowed are immediate family members.

cards.front: How do the first six licensed months and months seven through twelve differ for teen passengers?
cards.back: The first six licensed months allow only an instructor, a licensed parent or guardian, or one qualified twenty plus adult aboard, while months seven through twelve add immediate family and nobody else.

cards.front: During which hours may teens not drive, and what are the exceptions?
cards.back: Teens may not drive from eleven at night to five in the morning unless riding for a job, school, worship, medical need, or as an assigned Safe Ride driver.

cards.front: Who skips the teen passenger and curfew limits?
cards.back: Active volunteer fire, ambulance and emergency medical members answering or returning from calls, plus assigned Safe Ride drivers, skip the passenger and curfew limits.

cards.front: How does the volunteer emergency exemption relate to the curfew exceptions?
cards.back: The eleven to five night curfew binds teen drivers except for job, school, worship, medical or Safe Ride trips, and a separate exemption covers volunteer crews on emergency duty.

cards.front: What must permit holders and licensed sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds never do?
cards.back: Permit holders and licensed sixteen and seventeen year olds must never overload seatbelts, drive public passenger or vanpool vehicles, touch any phone or mobile device even hands free, or carry motorcycle passengers within six months of endorsement.

cards.front: Which bans apply to both permit holders and licensed teens?
cards.back: Overloading seatbelts, driving passenger or vanpool vehicles, touching any phone even hands free, and early motorcycle passengers are banned for both permit holders and licensed teens alike.

decks.domain: Licensing, road test and teen restrictions

cards.front: How do you sign up as an organ donor, and what does changing the choice later require?
cards.back: Organ donor sign up happens at licensing or renewal, online, or by mail, needs an appointment with current license or ID in hand, costs nothing, but changing the choice later needs a duplicate credential with a thirty dollar fee.

cards.front: What does the donor registry mean for adults of eighteen or more?
cards.back: For adults of eighteen or more the donor registry counts as legal donation authorization, so tell family and read more at ct.gov slash dmv.

cards.front: What does joining the donor registry cost compared with changing the choice later?
cards.back: Joining the donor registry costs nothing at licensing, but flipping the donor choice later demands a duplicate credential and a thirty dollar fee.

cards.front: How does DMV handle voter registration with license transactions?
cards.back: DMV offers voter registration or updates with every license transaction at any time, receipts and forwards the form, and a registrar confirmation should land in about three weeks, while an address change also moves the voter record unless declined.

cards.front: How do voter sign-up and an address change connect to license transactions?
cards.back: Voter sign up rides along any license transaction with a three week confirmation, and a plain address change moves the voter record too unless the driver opts out.

decks.domain: Licensing, road test and teen restrictions

cards.front: Whom does the limited license program serve, and on what basis?
cards.back: The limited license program serves drivers whose abilities changed since licensing and newcomers who now qualify, on physician reports and possibly an inspector road skills test.

cards.front: What should applicants with stable monitored conditions do, and how early?
cards.back: Stable monitored conditions may still allow driving, but affected applicants should call Driver Services at least four months early at (eight hundred sixty) two hundred sixty-three-five thousand seven hundred twenty-three.

cards.front: Which licenses carry higher health bars?
cards.back: Health bars run higher for commercial licenses and for licenses covering taxis, delivery vans, buses and school buses.

cards.front: What restrictions can a limited license carry?
cards.back: A limited license can restrict driving to daylight from a half hour before sunrise to a half hour after sunset, to corrective non telescopic lenses, to ordinary highways, to automatic gears, to dual mirror cars seeing two hundred feet back, or to special control cars.

cards.front: How do limited license curbs differ from the health bars for commercial and passenger licenses?
cards.back: Limited licenses add daylight, lens, highway, gear, mirror and equipment curbs for impaired drivers, while commercial and passenger licenses instead face tougher health bars.

cards.front: Where can disabled residents seek training to drive with adaptive gear?
cards.back: Disabled residents who might drive with adaptive gear can seek state training through the Bureau of Rehabilitation Services at (eight hundred sixty) four hundred twenty-four-four thousand eight hundred forty-four.
